Article Title: 'He can remove Pak from world picture': Shinde after Sharif crops PM Modi from SCO pic
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde criticised Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s Office for cropping Prime Minister Narendra Modi out of a photograph from the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, saying Pakistan should not attempt to “play such games” with India.“What Pakistan has done is extremely unfortunate. Pakistan has always attempted such things. However, I would say that while they may have removed Modi Ji’s photograph, if Modi Ji wants, he can remove Pakistan from the world picture,” Shinde said on Tuesday.His remarks came after Sharif’s office shared an edited version of the SCO family photograph that placed the Pakistani prime minister at the centre while cropping out several leaders. The original photograph, taken before a session of the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, showed the heads of member states standing together.“During Operation Sindoor, terrorists in Pahalgam committed a grave crime against our people and our sisters by wiping away their sindoor. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, our armed forces completely destroyed terrorist bases in Pakistan. They also destroyed 11 airbase camps and brought Pakistan to its knees,” he said.“The entire country is proud of the Indian armed forces and Prime Minister Modi’s leadership. Therefore, Pakistan should never attempt to play such games with our country,” Shinde added.He also said that editing Modi out of the photograph would not affect his standing in India or internationally.“I would also say that such an act of removing a photograph cannot erase Prime Minister Modi from the hearts of 140 crore Indians. In fact, Prime Minister Modi remains one of the most popular leaders in the world...”The 26th SCO summit, which marked the organisation’s 25th anniversary, focused on regional cooperation as well as security, economic and geopolitical challenges. The summit was held in the expanded “SCO Plus” format, bringing together leaders from member, partner and observer countries.Addressing the summit, PM Modi called for a united fight against terrorism and said there could be no “double standards” on the issue. He called for the dismantling of the “entire ecosystem of terrorism”, including its financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens.
Article Summary: Shinde's remarks came after sharif’s office shared an edited version of the sco family photograph. The original photograph, taken before a session of the 26th sco summit in bishkek, showed the heads of member states standing together.

Article Title: SC: Why not use 'totaliser' to mix votes?
Article Text:
Supreme Court Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes from different EVMs before counting, to prevent any backlash from candidates by preserving voter anonymity.Petitioner advocate Ashwini Upadhyay said a totalisation system hides booth-wise voting patterns by mixing up votes from multiple electronic voting machines (typically around 14) before displaying the count, which helps protect voters from post-poll violence and political victimisation. Election Commission , through senior advocate D Seshadri Naidu, said the issue was referred by EC to govt, which consulted stakeholders and found it inadvisable to employ the 'totalisation' mechanism, mainly because of staunch opposition by political parties. He said a switch to this method would require changing the statute which the commission could not bring about.When Upadhyay pointed out that the totalisation mechanism was adopted by EC to count paper ballots, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked Centre to respond on why the same mechanism could not be adopted for EVMs. Upadhyay also said in Jan 2018, EC itself had told the court that the "time had come" to introduce the totaliser to "protect secrecy of the ballot and privacy of the individual".It had said that "the right of the people staying in a particular locality should not be exposed, and any kind of prejudice or discrimination because of the voting pattern should be avoided".In a U-turn, EC in its affidavit filed on Aug 31 said, "Experience of litigations has revealed that the present system which includes a simultaneous audit by the candidates is necessary to ensure that frivolous and baseless allegations do not cloud the outcome..." It said the introduction of the totaliser system would give fresh anxieties, misgivings and allegations regarding data, machine tampering and transmission glitches.
Article Summary: Supreme court tuesday sought centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes from different evms. Election commission said the issue was referred by ec to govt, which consulted stakeholders and found it inadvisable to employ the 'totalisation' mechanism.

Article Title: Times Square stabbing: Bank of America VP Erin Piacenti among victims
Article Text:
NYPD commissioner Jessica Tisch said the attack appeared to be random and unprovoked. Police said officers arriving at the scene encountered Pamela Cisneros, 49, who was brandishing two large knives and advancing towards them

Who was Erin Piacenti?

How the incident unfolded

A 32-year-old vice-president at Bank of America was killed in a stabbing incident in New York’s Times Square. The attack, described by police as “random” and unprovoked, unfolded on Monday afternoon.The victim was identified as Erin Piacenti, who was walking home from work when she was attacked near West 42nd Street and Seventh Avenue. Piacenti had recently returned to work after becoming a mother and had shared a photo of herself with her newborn daughter and husband four days before the stabbing.A 68-year-old man was also stabbed in the attack and was in stable condition, according to police. The attacker, identified as 49-year-old Pamela Cisneros, was shot and killed by officers after she advanced towards them while carrying two large knives.Piacenti was a vice-president in Bank of America’s Business Selection and Conflicts unit and had joined the company around 18 months ago, according to an internal memo and her LinkedIn profile.Matthew Koder, Bank of America’s president of Global Corporate & Investment Banking, described Piacenti as a “cherished teammate and friend” in an internal memo.“Erin was a valued member of the Business Selection and Conflicts team, having joined the bank 18 months ago,” Koder wrote.“Her loss is being felt deeply by many.”Bank of America confirmed Piacenti’s death and expressed condolences to her family.“We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. Our hearts go out to her family and all of her loved ones,” the bank said in a statement.Piacenti had earned a law degree from Fordham Law School, graduating in 2021 alongside her husband, Frank, according to the school. Fordham Law said in a statement it was heartbroken by her death.Bank of America’s Manhattan office is located at One Bryant Park, just a few blocks from the site of the stabbing.NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the attack appeared to be random and unprovoked. Police identified the attacker as Pamela Cisneros, 49, of Queens.According to Tisch, Cisneros pulled two knives from a shopping bag, stabbed the 68-year-old man and then attacked Piacenti. When officers arrived, they found Cisneros brandishing two large knives and advancing towards them.Officers used a stun gun and tried to persuade her to drop the weapons for several minutes, but she refused. Tisch said Cisneros told officers she “would rather kill” them. Two officers then shot her, and she was later pronounced dead.Tisch said Cisneros had a documented mental health history, with police encounters related to mental health in 2018 and 2019, but no arrest record in New York City.Cisneros’ brother, Patrick Peralta, told Gothamist that she had psychiatric problems for decades but was not aggressive. He said she had been taking medication and had been doing better in recent years, working on and off in a legal office.“We really don’t know how to express or how to explain why this happened," Peralta told Gothamist, expressing sympathy for Piacenti’s family and the injured man.Koder said Bank of America’s security teams were “fully engaged in supporting the police investigation here, and in addressing the ongoing safety and security of our offices and teammates”.
Article Summary: Erin piacenti, a 32-year-old vice-president at bank of america, was killed in a stabbing incident in new york’s times square on monday afternoon. The victim was walking home from work when she was attacked near west 42nd street and seventh avenue.

Article Title: ‘Pre-event indications’: Did Nepal miss warning signs before deadly floods? What report says
Article Text:
A visual from the flash floods that has killed over 1,100

Also Read |

Warning signs before collapse?

Also Read |

Death toll rises to 1,127

Other reports also highlighted disaster possibility

The glacier collapse that triggered a devastating landslide and flash floods along the Nepal-China border, killing over 1,100 showed visible signs of instability days before the disaster, according to a new report by the HiRISK scientific consortium.Scientists said there were “pre-event indications”, including meltwater that had turned visibly brown and signs of a crack propagating into the surrounding bedrock slope.The findings have raised fresh questions over the lack of operational early warning systems for glacier-related hazards in the remote Himalayan region, with scientists saying more comprehensive systems downstream could have saved a “significant number of lives”.The HiRISK report, published last week, cited by CNN, examined the physical changes preceding the glacier collapse and the potential for early detection.“In hindsight, there were some pre-event indications,” the scientists said, pointing to visibly brown meltwater and a crack that was propagating into the surrounding bedrock slope days before the collapse.However, detecting such changes in a remote, high-altitude environment remains difficult.The report said early warning systems had recently been established in the region to monitor several glacial lakes in China, but no operational system was in place specifically for glacier-related hazards in the area where the collapse occurred.Once the collapse began, the speed of the initial landslide meant conventional warning systems would likely have provided too little time to evacuate a border checkpoint that was among the first areas hit.Further downstream, however, there may have been more time to respond.The scientists said comprehensive early warning systems capable of providing 10 minutes or more of advance notice could have saved a “significant number of lives”.The finding stressed the need for systems that can monitor not only glacial lakes but also unstable glaciers and surrounding mountain slopes, while ensuring warnings reach vulnerable communities downstream.As the cause and rescue ops continue, 1,127 people have died in the floods, according to Nepal Police. A total of 45 bodies have been recovered from Rasuwa, 155 from Nuwakot, 59 from Dhading, 348 from Chitwan, 66 from Gorkha, 38 from Tanahun, 217 from Nawalparasi East and 190 from Nawalparasi West.The death toll has risen to 1,127, with 45 bodies recovered in Rasuwa, 155 in Nuwakot, 59 in Dhading, 348 in Chitwan, 66 in Gorkha, 38 in Tanahun, 217 in Nawalparasi East and 190 in Nawalparasi West. Nine bodies have also been recovered in India. So far, only 95 of the total recovered bodies have been identified and handed over to their families.The disaster has also renewed calls for greater cooperation between Nepal and China in monitoring hazards across the Himalayas.Chinese and Nepali authorities had met as recently as May to discuss strengthening cooperation on monitoring natural hazards in the region, according to a government official who attended the meeting.Experts say better cross-border information sharing is particularly important because mountain hazards can rapidly affect communities and infrastructure on either side of the border.“There is almost no way that anyone could have detected this event prior – it happened in a blind spot … (making it) extremely difficult to detect,” Austin Lord, a senior fellow in the Energy, Water and Sustainability programme at the Stimson Center, wrote in a recent commentary.He also highlighted “how greater communication, information sharing, and collaborative analysis of transboundary risks between Nepal and China are sorely needed.”India also stepped up to assist Nepal’s rescue operations, deploying specialised Army teams to work alongside Nepali forces at the Chilime and Langtang tunnel sites. The teams have been navigating difficult terrain and unstable conditions as they search for missing people.Read more: India steps in with emergency helplines for stranded nationals The HiRISK report is separate from two major reports released by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) in March 2026.The ICIMOD reports examined longer-term changes across the Hindu Kush Himalaya and warned that accelerating glacier loss was increasing the risks of cryosphere-related hazards, including glacial lake outburst floods.They found that HKH glaciers lost around 12 per cent of their total area and 9 per cent of their estimated ice reserves between 1990 and 2020, while glacier ice loss had doubled after 2000.The reports also found that the region’s smallest glaciers were shrinking particularly rapidly, with three-fourths of HKH glaciers falling into the vulnerable category of less than 0.5 square kilometres.ICIMOD also highlighted major gaps in glacier monitoring. Its 2026 Glacier Outlook found that only seven of 38 monitored glaciers met the global benchmark monitoring standards set by the World Glacier Monitoring Service, while several major glacierised regions remained largely unmonitored.“This isn’t a distant problem; it’s a crisis unfolding in real-time, with new disasters every summer and monsoon,” ICIMOD Director General Pema Gyamtsho said.Thus, the ICIMOD reports provided a broad assessment of the region’s accelerating glacier loss and the risks it creates, while the new HiRISK report focuses specifically on the recent disaster, including the physical warning signs before the collapse and whether early warning systems could have reduced casualties.
Article Summary: Scientists said there were “pre-event indications’, including meltwater that had turned visibly brown and signs of a crack propagating into the surrounding bedrock slope. The findings have raised fresh questions over the lack of operational early warning systems for glacier-related hazards in the remote himalayan region.

Article Title: Pak takes SCO chair, PM Modi slams use of terror as strategic asset
Article Text:
Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy must be sent a strong message

Framing security as a non-negotiable prerequisite for regional progress, PM Narendra Modi delivered a thinly veiled warning to Pakistan over state-sponsored terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. With Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif in attendance, Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone.The remarks are significant also because of the timing. Pakistan assumed rotating chairmanship of SCO from Kyrgyzstan on Tuesday and will host the heads-of-state summit next year, for which it will invite Modi, along with others.Modi made the remarks, in which he also warned against double standards on terrorism, while expanding on India's SCO vision - Security, Connectivity and Opportunity - that he articulated in Tianjin last year.With Chinese President Xi Jinping also present, PM reiterated India's position that all connectivity initiatives must respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states as this is also the "fundamental spirit" of SCO charter.Modi said that terrorism continued to pose a serious challenge to humanity and it's important to not remain confined to an action-reaction approach in the fight against the menace.“We must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation, and safe havens. We must speak with one voice and make it clear that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue,” said PM, without naming Pakistan as SCO charter doesn’t allow members to raise bilateral differences.India and Pakistan together joined the China-dominated Eurasian grouping as full members in 2017. For India, the security-oriented SCO has served as a platform not just to assert its strategic autonomy but also flag regional risks from state-sponsored terrorism. Modi said that the bloc’s shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also closely linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan and that India will continue to contribute to the development and provision of humanitarian assistance to people of the country.Modi addressed West Asia crisis, saying it was affecting energy security, maritime trade and supply chains around the world and recalling his message earlier that conflicts cannot be resolved on the battlefield. “Countries of Global South bear greatest brunt of such disruptions. Therefore, India has consistently called for all tensions and conflicts to be resolved not on battlefield, but through dialogue and diplomacy,” he added.While underlining the importance India attaches to SCO, Modi said that at a time when the world is passing through instability, the organisation must transform the shared geography into opportunities and bring about positive change in people’s lives. Describing SCO as a confluence of great civilisations, cultures, and ideas, he said that over next 25 years, people-to-people ties should remain at the heart of cooperation among the member states.“True measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts create, how many new markets open up for entrepreneurs, how much farmers benefit from tech, and how much better the lives of our citizens become,” said the PM. According to an Indian readout of PM’s participation, Modi stated that strong and trusted connectivity initiatives were important for the group’s shared progress and prosperity.“Underlining that India supports connectivity efforts that link markets, enhance trade and open new opportunities for development, he reiterated such efforts should respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of nations,” said the readout.
Article Summary: Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy must be sent a strong message. Pakistan assumed rotating chairmanship of sco from kyrgyzstan on tuesday. India and pakistan together joined the china-dominated eurasian grouping as full members in 2017.

Article Title: PM Modi repeats call to 'shun unnecessary gold buys, foreign weddings & holidays'
Article Text:
PM Modi on Tuesday lauded Indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises

NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the better-than-expected GDP growth, PM Modi on Tuesday lauded Indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises. He again pushed for swadeshi goods and urged citizens to shun overseas weddings, foreign vacations and avoid unnecessary gold purchases at a time when imports remain elevated due to high commodity prices in the wake of the West Asia conflict.His appeal against buying gold also puts to rest speculation around import duties being reviewed by govt. In fact, Centre and RBI are keeping a close watch on shipments. Since Jan, both quantity of gold and value of imports have increased. Since Modi's first appeal in May, however, there has been a drop in quantity of imports but the value of imports is rising due to higher prices, albeit at a slower pace. At $3.5 a kg, the unit value of gold was 94% higher in June, but prices have moderated to $2.8 a kg, which was 47% more than a year ago.Since Modi’s first appeal in May, gold import quantity has dropped, but import value is rising due to higher prices, albeit slower. Prices moderated to $2.8 a kg, 47% more than a year ago.While gold remains an investment option for households, higher prices have deterred consumers from buying large quantities, with recycling of old jewellery also rising, industry executives said.Modi also mounted a withering attack on LoP Rahul Gandhi for spreading pessimism about growth, dismissing his criticism as “jhooth ki goonj”.This was Modi’s second reaction to the growth rate within 24 hours. His message mixed praise for people’s hard work with disdain for critics like Rahul and reiterated his call to citizens to avoid non-essential gold purchases and foreign trips.“We have to maintain this pace and keep growing and, for this, aatmanirbhar Bharat is essential,” he said in a selfie-video posted on Instagram.GDP grew at 7.8% in the April-June quarter, bringing relief to the NDA govt, which has been buffeted by the opposition parties, especially Congress under Rahul, over alleged misgovernance. Modi said, “There are people within India who are mired in despair, ‘jhooth ki goonj’, and are busy spreading pessimism everywhere.”Emphasising India’s feat, Modi said it came amid global conflicts and crises, causing supply-chain disruption. Since Covid in 2020, stability has remained elusive for the world but India is progressing at a fast pace, he added.Opposition has a right to criticise govt but especially Congress shouldn’t insult people by being incorrigible naysayers and call India a dead economy when data speaks otherwise, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said.BJP played up Rahul’s dismissive comments about the economy to contrast them with India’s growth. Besides his dead economy jibe, Rahul claimed a crisis unseen in people’s lifetime would hit the economy. An economic tsunami was coming, he had said. Modi said his govt’s policy is right and intentions clear, calling upon people to work hard. India’s collective strength will take it to new heights. By emphasising swadeshi and self-reliance, people will bequeath a developed India to the young generation.At a press conference, BJP’s Ravi Shankar Prakash demanded Rahul apologise. As leader of opposition, Rahul’s comments carry weight, he said. The world has begun taking them lightly as he makes misleading remarks, while Pakistan plays them up.
Article Summary: Pm modi on tuesday lauded indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises. He again pushed for swadeshi goods and urged citizens to shun overseas weddings, foreign vacations and avoid unnecessary gold purchases. Since modi's first appeal in may, there has been a drop in quantity of imports but the value of imports is rising due to higher prices, albeit slower.

Article Title: From marble inlay, silk to Mahabharata: What PM Modi gifted Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan leaders at SCO summit

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who participated in the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic, presented a range of traditional Indian handicrafts, textiles, tea, musical instruments and literary works to leaders and dignitaries from Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan.The gifts showcased India's diverse cultural heritage while highlighting the country's longstanding cultural and diplomatic ties with Central Asia.Modi gifted president of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev a marble inlay decorative plate, featuring floral and foliate motifs in blue, green and red set into polished white marble. The craft is particularly associated with Agra in Uttar Pradesh and reflects generations of Indian artisan skill.The Prime Minister also presented Mirziyoyev with two boxes of premium Kangra tea, Kangra First Flush Black Tea and Kangra Green Tea, housed in a carved wooden box. The tea represents the heritage of Kangra Valley in Himachal Pradesh, where cultivation dates back to the 19th century.Another gift was a sandalwood Shata Tantri Veena, popularly known as the Santoor, a many-stringed instrument associated with Jammu and Kashmir.Its resemblance to Uzbekistan's traditional Chang was highlighted as a link between the musical traditions of the two countries.Modi also presented Mirziyoyev with the original handwritten scoresheet of Uzbek Grandmaster Javokhir Sindarov from the 2025 FIDE World Cup final in Goa. Sindarov defeated China's Wei Yi to become the youngest FIDE World Cup champion and qualify for the 2026 Candidates Tournament.Uzbekistan Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov received a marble inlay decorative plate, showcasing India's traditional stone-inlay craftsmanship and intricate floral designs.He was also gifted a marble inlay casket with a Banarasi silk stole. The white marble casket carries floral patterns created with coloured stones, while the blue Banarasi silk stole features a paisley zari design, bringing together craft traditions from Agra and Varanasi.PM Modi gifted Uzbekistan president’s spouse and first lady Ziroat Mirziyoyeva, a marble inlay casket paired with a Banarasi silk stole, blending Agra’s stone craftsmanship with Varanasi’s weaving heritage. The floral marble work and blue paisley zari design reflected India’s artistic traditions.Modi gifted the daughter of Uzbekistan's president a fine silver brooch featuring a floral bouquet in an ornamental basket. The piece incorporates openwork, latticework, leaves, blossoms, green cabochons and clear stones.For the prime minister of Kyrgyzstan, Modi presented a Dokra artwork depicting a pair of traditional musicians. The handcrafted pieces use India's traditional lost-wax metal-casting technique.Meanwhile, Kyrgyzstan's president was gifted a Ladakhi Tsug-dul blanket, a traditional woollen textile from Ladakh featuring geometric, floral and stylised motifs.A 10-volume English translation of the Mahabharata by Bibek Debroy was also presented to the president.Together, the gifts showcased India's regional crafts, artistic traditions, literature and cultural heritage while underscoring the longstanding cultural affinities between India and Central Asia.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi presented gifts to leaders and dignitaries from uzbekistan and kyrgyzstan. The gifts showcased india's diverse cultural heritage while highlighting the country's longstanding cultural and diplomatic ties with central asia. Modi participated in the 26th meeting of the council of heads of state of the shanghai cooperation organisation (sco)

Article Title: India on board, SCO reiterates condemnation of Iran attacks
Article Text:
SCO member-states, including India, reiterated the bloc's condemnation of military strikes on Iranian territory

India also joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Expressing deep concern over developments in "the Middle East and around Iran", the SCO member-states including India reiterated the bloc's condemnation of military strikes on Iranian territory that resulted in numerous civilian casualties and significant damage to Iran's economy, said the Bishkek Declaration.India also joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei.This was the second time that the SCO denounced the strikes on Iran after the West Asia war started on February 28, the first in an early March standalone statement that called the attacks unacceptable. India had endorsed that statement too, even though bilaterally it has not explicitly condemned the attacks on Iran the way it has missile and drone strikes on the GCC countries.However, unlike the Tianjin Declaration last year that too condemned the June 2025 US and Israeli strikes on Iran, the Bishkek Declaration did not name the US and Israel."Such actions violate the principles and norms of international law and the UN Charter and create serious risks to international peace, security and stability," said SCO's Bishkek Declaration.India and others backed Iran's sovereignty and territorial integrity, advocating a resolution to the conflict solely through political and diplomatic means.In this regard, they welcome all efforts aimed at de-escalating the situation in the region and, as the declaration said, noted that the only possible way to ensure peace and stability in the Middle East is a comprehensive and just settlement of the Palestinian question.PM Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek on Monday and backed expansion of bilateral economic ties with Tehran, while the Iranian president sought India's help to end the war. After distancing itself from a statement by SCO in June last year condemning Israel's strikes, India has signed on to joint documents by the bloc censuring US-Israel military action against Iran.The Declaration reflected a major Indian concern as it strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, emphasised that "double standards" in the fight against terrorism are unacceptable, and called on the international community to combat terrorism, including the cross-border movement of terrorists.It called for the UN playing a central role by fully implementing relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy in accordance with the UN Charter and the principles of international law to jointly combat all terrorist groups."Member States, reaffirming their firm commitment to combating terrorism, separatism, and extremism, emphasize the inadmissibility of attempts to exploit terrorist, separatist, and extremist groups for selfish purposes. They recognize the leading role of sovereign states and their competent authorities in countering terrorist and extremist threats," said the Declaration.Significantly, targeting use of economic sanctions by the West, the leaders came out in support of an open, fair and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system focused heavily on the framework established by the WTO, while slamming unilateral coercive measures."Member States oppose unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to the UN Charter and other norms of international law, the rules and principles of the World Trade Organization, that are detrimental to the interests of ensuring international security, including its food, energy and humanitarian components, and that have a negative impact on the global economy," said the Bishkek Declaration.
Article Summary: Sco member-states, including india, reiterated the bloc's condemnation of military strikes on iranian territory. India also joined other member- states in expressing condolences over the death of former iranian supreme leader ali khamenei. This was the second time that the sco denounced the strikes on iran after the west asia war started on february 28.

Article Title: India's GDP growth: BJP hails 'economic resilience'; Congress asks where are the jobs?
Article Text:
Prasad compared India’s performance with growth recorded by several other major economies while Khera argued that a single quarter of strong GDP growth should not be treated as evidence of broad-based economic prosperity.

NEW DELHI: The BJP and Congress on Tuesday traded sharply contrasting assessments of India’s economy after official data showed GDP growth of 7.8 per cent in the April-June 2026 quarter. While the BJP hailed the performance as evidence of resilient economic management, the Opposition questioned whether the growth has translated into jobs, higher incomes and wider prosperity.BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad held a press conference where he described the latest growth figures as “particularly significant”. He argued that India had expanded rapidly despite heightened geopolitical and economic uncertainty during the quarter, including the Gulf crisis, disruptions to oil supplies and supply-chain pressures.“Today is a very encouraging day. The latest report shows that India’s GDP growth stood at 7.8 per cent in the April-June 2026 quarter. The figure of 7.8 per cent is particularly significant because, during this period, the Gulf crisis had intensified. There were concerns over oil supplies, disruptions in supply chains, and uncertainty across the global economy. Despite all these challenges, India’s economy grew by 7.8 per cent,” Prasad said at a press conference in Delhi.Prasad also compared India’s performance with growth recorded by several other major economies, saying Canada grew by around 1.5 per cent, Germany by 1 per cent, the UK by 2.1 per cent, Malaysia by about 6 per cent, South Korea by around 3.7 per cent and the US by roughly 2 per cent during the same period.He attributed India’s performance to what he called effective economic management and praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership.“Today, I would like to congratulate and commend India’s economic management. I also wholeheartedly congratulate the honourable Prime Minister for his vision, wisdom and leadership,” Prasad said.The Congress, however, challenged the BJP’s interpretation of the GDP figures, arguing that headline growth alone does not adequately capture the economic conditions faced by ordinary Indians.Congress leader Pawan Khera questioned how the 7.8 per cent growth figure was benefiting young people and farmers, while also pointing to concerns over employment, manufacturing, education and income distribution.“The Prime Minister comes up with a reel, a video. Ask him: the largest demographic in this country is the youth. How does this GDP growth affect the youth? How does it address the issues that young people face? The largest occupation in this country is agriculture. How does this GDP growth affect the agricultural sector? If it doesn’t benefit these two sectors, how does it affect the dwindling manufacturing sector? Look at the manufacturing data. So, what is he even talking about? A handful of people contribute to the growth of this country, but where is the redistribution of income? Where is the distribution of income? So, let’s talk about these fundamental issues. 80 per cent of this country depends on free ration. Is that what good GDP growth does for the country? That’s our question.”Khera had earlier taken his criticism to X, arguing that a single quarter of strong GDP growth should not be treated as evidence of broad-based economic prosperity.“One quarter of 7.8% growth is not an economic spring. If India has truly "bloomed," why do rampant unemployment, leaked exam papers, and a crumbling education system define the ground reality? Why is the republic's prosperity not translating into the prosperity of its public? GDP measures national output - not jobs, not wages, not opportunity. If it measured any of those, the future of India's youth would not look so bleak. Modi can manage his headlines. For India's youth, the question remains the same as ever: Where are the jobs?”At his press conference, Khera also questioned whether the strong GDP reading had resulted in tangible improvements in the cost of living and employment conditions.“On one hand, they say, "Look at the GDP of a single quarter and applaud." On the other, they say, "Don't buy gold, don't host lavish weddings." They themselves sit abroad while telling the country's citizens not to travel overseas and to save money. 80% of the population relies on free rations, but keep applauding... Regarding this 7.8% figure—what benefit is the country's largest sector, agriculture, deriving from it? The youth constitute the country's largest demographic; what benefit are they getting? Have their issues been resolved? Have milk prices dropped? Is there no longer a need for free rations? Have you rectified the employment situation to reverse the 45-year record low? Is manufacturing back on track? What happened to the MSME sector? What happened to the unorganized sector? If you have answers showing a positive outcome, then we, too, will applaud...”The competing responses underline the political divide over how India's economic performance should be assessed. While the BJP has used the 7.8 per cent quarterly expansion to highlight India's relative resilience amid global disruptions, the Congress has focused on whether headline GDP growth is being reflected in employment, household incomes and opportunities for India's young population.

Opposition questioned whether growth has translated into jobs, higher incomes and wider prosperity. For india's youth, the question remains the same as ever: where are the jobs?

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said there can be no “double standards” in the fight against terrorism and called for dismantling its entire ecosystem, including financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens.Addressing the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, PM Modi described terrorism as a “grave challenge to all of humanity” and said the fight against it cannot be limited to a mindset of “action-reaction”.“We must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism--its financing, recruitment, radicalization, and safe havens. We must speak in one voice that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue,” he said.“Those countries that use terrorism as an instrument of their policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism cannot be a ‘strategic asset’ for anyone,” the Prime Minister added.He also outlined "Security, Connectivity and Opportunity" as the three pillars of India’s vision for the SCO, with peace and security forming the first pillar.“Our shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan,” he said, adding that India would continue its development and humanitarian assistance to the Afghan people.On the West Asia crisis, Modi said conflicts in one region can have repercussions across the world, affecting “energy security, maritime trade, and supply chains of the entire world”.“The countries of the Global South have to bear the maximum brunt of this. Therefore, India's call has been that the solution to all tensions and wars is not possible on the battlefield, but only through Dialogue and Diplomacy,” he said.The Prime Minister also flagged drug trafficking as a serious threat to the younger generation and regional security, calling for stronger cooperation through SCO mechanisms dealing with security threats, organised crime, information security and narcotics. “We must make them effective mediums for practical coordination and timely action,” PM Modi said.He further stressed that SCO cooperation should translate into tangible benefits for people, with people-to-people ties placed at the centre of the grouping’s future agenda.“The true measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts have created for young people, how many new markets have opened up for our entrepreneurs, how much our farmers have benefited from technology, and how much better the lives of our citizens have become,” he said.Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov is hosting the summit and serving as its chairman. Article Title: Kenney, Sikh leader share dais as Bhagwat makes global Hindu call
Article Text:
Bhagwat’s visit came despite demands from New Democratic Party and civil-society groups that he be denied entry to Canada. The venue was disclosed shortly before the programme amid security concerns.

NEW DELHI: A day after telling a New York audience that a Hindu who wanted Muslims excluded from India could not remain a Hindu, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat Monday used his first visit to Canada to cast Hindus as builders of an “exemplary society” worldwide and India as a “vishwaguru” serving humanity, not a “mahashakti” seeking dominance.The speeches shared themes of oneness, but differed in emphasis. In New York, amid protests and criticism of RSS, Bhagwat addressed concerns about exclusion; in Toronto, he explained how Hindu society should organise and lead internationally without imposing its beliefs.“The word Hindu cannot be defined by any specific language, through any specific worship or through any living style,” he said. The dais reflected that wider outreach: former Alberta premier and federal cabinet minister Jason Kenney and Kashmir Singh Dhaliwal of the Khalsa Diwan Society joined Bhagwat, placing a senior Canadian political figure and a representative of a Sikh institution alongside the RSS chief at a gathering opposed by sections of the South Asian community.“We have to build our society in every country, all over the world, which is an exemplary society for the world,” Bhagwat said at the “Hindu Vishwa Bandhu — Embrace the World in Friendship” event. The programme in Vaughan, in the Greater Toronto Area, was organised by Canadian Hindus for Outreach, Relations and Dialogue.Presenting India’s global role as one based on service rather than power, Bhagwat said: “It became ‘vishwaguru’, not ‘mahashakti’.”Whenever help had been sought during an international crisis, he said, India had not refused. “This is the tradition. This is the DNA of Bharat.”Bhagwat said the RSS organised Hindus “exactly for this purpose — and nothing else”, describing the purpose as developing individuals who would dedicate themselves to serving humanity.The RSS chief coupled the call for organisation with a message on civic responsibility. People connected with India but settled elsewhere, he said, “have to be honest, contributing citizens of that country”. At the same time, they should take to the world an outlook in which individuals, society and the environment could progress without harming one another.He said this should be done through conduct rather than imposition. “We don’t force,” Bhagwat said. “We are the leaders who lead from within and lead by example.” He added: “Hindus respect all. Hindus accept all.”Going beyond the familiar expression “unity in diversity”, Bhagwat said Hindu tradition also recognised “diversities of unity”. Different identities, he argued, were expressions of an underlying oneness. “Diversity is never a problem for unity,” he said. “All the diversities are expressions of unity.”Bhagwat’s visit came despite demands from New Democratic Party and civil-society groups that he be denied entry to Canada. The venue was disclosed shortly before the programme amid security concerns.

Article Title: 'A particular issue': Penguin India on impasse over Sonia Gandhi memoir
Article Text:
PRHI declined to reveal the nature of the disputed issue, citing its contractual obligations and commitment to author confidentiality.

NEW DELHI: Penguin Random House India on Monday said publication of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir in India had stalled after the publisher and the author’s representatives reached an “impasse over a particular issue. ” The publisher also firmly denied that any external pressure had influenced the decision.Penguin India said the disagreement emerged during its normal editorial review of Belonging: A Journey of Love, which it had been keen to publish.The clarification came amid a growing political controversy over the memoir’s India publication, after Alfred A Knopf, the US-based imprint of Penguin Random House, announced that the book would be released worldwide on November 10. While Congress leaders have raised questions about possible governmental pressure and freedom of expression, Penguin India said the disagreement was strictly part of the editorial process.“On some, they agreed to changes and on others, we accepted the author’s position. Unfortunately, and ultimately, an understanding could not be reached on a particular issue,” the publisher said.PRHI spokesperson Pallavi Narayan said the publishing house had been “really keen” to bring out the memoir, describing it as “a hard-won acquisition”.“We feel it is important for us to correct certain misrepresentations regarding the forthcoming memoir 'Belonging'. This is a book that we at Penguin Random House India, were really keen on publishing as it was a hard-won acquisition,” Narayan said in an exclusive statement to PTI.The publisher said the manuscript had gone through its “normal editorial process”, during which several points were raised and discussed with the author’s representatives. Some proposed changes were accepted, while on other matters Penguin India accepted the author’s position.It was ultimately the unresolved issue that brought the publication process to a halt, according to PRHI. The author’s team subsequently informed the publisher that they did not wish to proceed with the publication, a decision the publishing house said it respected.At the same time, Penguin India rejected suggestions that the impasse was the result of intervention from outside the publishing process.“Since the content of the book is confidential and under embargo, there was no external pressure whatsoever,” the publisher said.PRHI declined to reveal the nature of the disputed issue, citing its contractual obligations and commitment to author confidentiality.“Since we are bound by an agreement, and author confidentiality is paramount to us, we will not divulge details of what led to the impasse,” the publisher said.The publishing house also defended its decision to scrutinise the manuscript, saying editorial assessment, questioning, fact-checking and recommendations were part of its responsibility as a publisher.“As publishers, it was its “responsibility and duty” to critically assess a manuscript, ask questions, make recommendations and exercise its independent editorial judgement,” Penguin India said.The controversy intensified after reports that Penguin India had backed out of publishing the memoir following disagreements over editorial changes. Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot alleged that pressure had been put on Penguin India to remove sections concerning Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the RSS and China’s occupation of Indian territory during the Modi government.Former Madhya Pradesh chief minister Kamal Nath also questioned whether the publisher’s position had been influenced by pressure from elsewhere.Penguin India’s latest statement, however, maintains that no such external intervention took place and that the disagreement arose solely during the editorial process.The memoir is expected to offer a rare account of Gandhi’s life, covering her childhood in post-war Italy, her marriage into the Nehru-Gandhi family, the assassination of her husband and former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, and her subsequent entry into politics.While the international edition is scheduled for release on November 10, the status of its publication in India remains unresolved.
Article Summary: Penguin random house india said publication of sonia gandhi’s memoir in india had stalled after the publisher and the author's representatives reached an “impasse over a particular issue” the publisher also firmly denied that any external pressure had influenced the decision.

Article Title: India & China announce 8-point boundary consensus before Xi's visit, target early & substantial harvest in border delimitation
Article Text:
According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly.

NEW DELHI: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question - co-chaired by Ajit Doval and Wang Yi this week - had led to an 8-point consensus, signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month.These included advancing consultations for an "early and substantial harvest" of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, expanding trans-border trade and rivers cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the SR talks.Building upon the outcomes from the last round of talks in 2024, the 2 sides agreed that the Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management would advance discussions on an “Early and Substantial Harvest” of boundary delimitation and Border Management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective Terms of Reference, said the joint statement.India and China had agreed last year to set up an expert group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC), to explore early harvest in boundary delimitation in the India-China border areas.The formulation was changed to early and substantial on this occasion.Two additional meeting points for military talks and 2 more channels of border military hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors were agreed upon to reinforce border management measures, according to both sides.“The two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR Talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution,” said the MEA in a statement. Unlike the Chinese readout of the talks on Tuesday, the joint statement did not mention package settlement or solution, although the 2005 agreement talks about making adjustments to reach a package settlement.The two sides also reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the guidance received from Modi and Xi, maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas and creating an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations.According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. “The two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management,” said the joint statement.Both sides also noted the progress on trans-border cooperation, with the Indian side appreciating the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Indian official pilgrimage Kailash-Manasarovar Yatra (KMY) in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.“Both sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with the view to work together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas,” said the joint statement.India and China also agreed to hold the next meeting of the India-China Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in September and maintain communication on issues including hydrological data sharing, and renewal of the relevant MoUs. It’s important for India that China shares hydrological information during emergency situations based on humanitarian considerations. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India in 2027.
Article Summary: India and china announced wednesday that the special representatives (sr) dialogue on the boundary question had led to an 8-point consensus. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the sr talks. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of sr talks in india in 2027.

Article Title: Hong Kong’s pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty to association with foreign entities
Article Text:
Pro-democratic student activist Joshua Wong, on Sept. 2, 2015. (Photo: AP)

Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong, 29, pleaded guilty on Wednesday to a national security allegation of collusion with foreign entities, an offence that carries a potential life sentence. Several Western diplomats were present at the hearing.Wong rose to international prominence as a teenage pro-democracy activist, part of a generation of young protesters whose activism has since been effectively criminalised under the sweeping National Security Law that Beijing imposed on Hong Kong in 2020.According to a charge sheet seen by Reuters, prosecutors accused Wong of conspiring with exiled activist Nathan Law and others to solicit foreign countries, institutions, organisations, or individuals to impose sanctions or blockades against Hong Kong and China. The alleged conduct occurred between July 1 and November 23, 2020. Wong was arrested on these charges in June 2025, the second time he has faced prosecution under the National Security Law.During the hearing, prosecutors emphasised an alleged international media and political campaign led by Demosisto, a now-disbanded political party Wong once led, that had advocated for a referendum on Hong Kong's sovereignty.The campaign reportedly sought sanctions against Hong Kong and China in 2019 and 2020.Wong is currently serving a sentence from an earlier national security conviction, conspiracy to commit subversion, stemming from his participation in an unofficial 2020 primary election among democratic activists. That sentence is due to end next year.The National Security Law was enacted on June 30, 2020, partly in response to the often-violent pro-democracy protests that engulfed Hong Kong in 2019.International human rights organisations and Western governments have criticised the law as excessive, arguing it undermines the high degree of autonomy promised to Hong Kong after its 1997 handover from British to Chinese rule.Hong Kong and Chinese authorities, however, maintain the law was necessary to restore stability.
Article Summary: Joshua wong, 29, pleaded guilty to a national security allegation of collusion with foreign entities. The offence carries a potential life sentence. Wong rose to international prominence as a teenage pro-democracy activist. His activism has since been effectively criminalised under the sweeping national security law.

US Vice President JD Vance said in a podcast released Tuesday (local time) that he feared a “real civil strife” had a 2024 attempt on Donald Trump ’s life been successful.Vance made the remarks during a conversation with Christian podcaster Bryce Crawford. Article Title: 'Stop doing memes': Canada's Mark Carney hits back at US as trade fight intensifies
Article Text:
US-Canada trade talks coallpsed in August

(With AP inputs)

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday (local time) hit back at the US, saying it should “stop doing memes, stop throwing shade and stop trying to be tough,” as he pushed back against a fresh wave of online barbs from the Trump administration, days after trade talks between the two sides collapsed.Carney also said trade talks could resume if Washington became “serious” about negotiations.“When the Americans stop doing memes, stop throwing shade and stop trying to be tough, and start being serious about having those discussions, we can have those discussions. It’s not constructive, but that’s their democracy,” he told reporters.The Canadian premier described the US approach in the talks as one that would have left Canadian industries effectively as "subsidiaries" of American companies or imposed terms under which they would be “gradually wound down in Canada and wiped out.”“We’re not going to — of course, we’re not going to accept those terms,” he said.Carney further stated that the US sought an “uncompetitive” deal for key industries, including autos, while also pushing changes affecting French-language and cultural protections. He argued that any one of those issues would have been enough to block an agreement.Washington also sought limits on Canada’s future trade deals, Carney noted.“Canada is a sovereign state. We will strike free trade deals with the countries we wish to strike free trade deals,” he asserted.Still, Carney acknowledged that there had been “mutually beneficial” elements to a potential deal before the talks broke down.His comments came amid a fresh barrage of criticism from Washington following the collapse of trade talks on August 21. Trump has since moved to rename Lake Ontario “Lake America” and taunted Canada on social media, while US treasury secretary Scott Bessent warned that Canada could not go “tit for tat” with an economy “13 times larger.”US secretary of war Pete Hegseth also mocked the Canadian military online, posting an image Monday of two female cadets at a training center in British Columbia alongside the words “this is real” and a Canadian flag. Carney described the post as “beneath their office.” The Pentagon, however, stood by the post Tuesday, saying, “The X post speaks for itself.”The trade talks broke down after the two sides failed to reach an agreement, prompting Trump to impose 50% tariffs on roughly $20 billion worth of Canadian goods. Ottawa’s retaliatory tariffs on nearly $20 billion in US goods are scheduled to take effect September 8, with duties ranging from 15% to 50%.Trump has repeatedly talked about making Canada the "51st US state" since returning to the White House in January 2025.
Article Summary: Us-canada trade talks coallpsed in august after the two sides failed to reach an agreement. President trump has since moved to rename lake ontario “lake america’ and taunted canada on social media. Article Title: Can Shilo Sanders escape the $11.89M judgment in his security guard case? Analyst reveals why Deion Sanders’ testimony could be crucial
Article Text:
Can Shilo Sanders escape the $11.89M judgment in his security guard case? Analyst reveals why Deion Sanders’ testimony could be crucial﻿(Getty)

Shilo Sanders faces a tough road after witnesses testify against him

Deion Sanders could provide key testimony in his son’s bankruptcy fight

Shilo Sanders is fighting to erase an $11.89 million judgment tied to a 2015 altercation with former school security guard John Darjean. His bankruptcy trial began on August 31 in Denver, and the early testimony has not helped his case. Now, attention has turned to his father, Deion Sanders, who could testify remotely before the trial ends.The case does not decide whether Shilo Sanders owes the money. A Texas court already entered the $11.89 million default judgment in Darjean’s favor in 2022. Instead, the bankruptcy judge must decide whether Shilo’s actions caused a “willful and malicious” injury. That ruling will determine whether he can wipe out the debt through bankruptcy.The case goes back to September 17, 2015, when Darjean worked as a security guard at Shilo’s school in Dallas. Darjean said he tried to take Shilo Sanders phone and accused the teenager of hitting and punching him during the confrontation.Shilo’s lawyers now argue that he acted in self-defense. That argument matters because bankruptcy law does not allow someone to erase a debt tied to a willful and malicious injury.The first day of the trial, however, gave Darjean’s side some momentum. On August 31, several witnesses testified through prerecorded video. One witness said Shilo struck Darjean with an elbow before punching him twice. Another described the attack as unprovoked, while another called Shilo’s behavior “aggressive” and “volatile,” according to Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk.That puts more weight on the defense’s version of events. Shilo’s lawyers must now convince Judge Michael E. Romero that the evidence supports self-defense rather than a deliberate attack.Deion Sanders could add another piece to that argument. Darjean has said he spoke with Deion by phone shortly before the confrontation and that the phone seizure happened at Deion’s direction.
